statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail stays in the 20-24 band as the session low holds for a third consecutive clock-hour while volatility and both yield tenors ease.
recommendation: Tail at 22 maps to WATCH, one point above the previous hour because the 19:00Z power hour and the 20:00Z cash close are still ahead. The narrow danger window is 19:00Z to 20:30Z, covering the power hour, the close and its settlement. A cash close beneath the 30,556.40 session low is the stated invalidation of this reading. Existing-position management and protective logic are unaffected by this mapped state.
headline: Session low holds for a third clock-hour as volatility and both yield tenors ease, keeping Tail in the watch band against high Stress
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index trades at 30,710.45, down 449.63 points or 1.44%, inside a 30,556.40 to 31,125.13 session range against a 31,160.08 previous close. Nasdaq-100 December futures, the preferred continuous reference, are at 30,904.00, down 1.59%, with a 30,792.50 session low; QQQ at 746.54, down 1.48% against a 743.23 low, corroborates the same structure from a third independent feed. The decisive observation for this hour is that the low set near 17:20Z has now held for more than two hours. The index sits roughly 154 points, about 0.50%, above it, the futures about 111 points above theirs, and the PHLX Semiconductor Index at 12,587.82, down 3.66%, about 104 points above its 12,483.95 low. Price has given back roughly half of the earlier bounce without printing a fresh extreme, which is a fading retracement inside a range, not the repeated extension after failed retracements that this provider's contract treats as Tail evidence. The macro amplifier stack has continued to unwind while that give-back developed. The ten-year Treasury yield is 5.23, down about five basis points on the day, near its 5.22 session low, eleven basis points below the 5.33 session high and some thirteen below the 5.356 twenty-four-year high reached on October 7. The two-year is 4.751, also lower on the day and near its own 4.743 session low, which is notable because it followed hawkish remarks rather than preceding them: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller told the Istanbul Economic Forum that he anticipates further increases to return inflation to the 2% target, with flexibility on timing and no need for consecutive meetings, against core PCE inflation of 3% in August, September payrolls up 29,000, unemployment at 4.2%, and a policy rate already lifted 25 basis points in September to 3.75-4%. The front end easing into that message is evidence the rate channel is absorbing rather than amplifying. The VIX is 15.61, up 3.51% but below 16, lower than the 15.88 printed an hour ago and off its own 16.46 session high; a volatility surface that decays through the afternoon is not the structure that accompanies a pathological one-way path. Breadth is the clearest argument against Tail. This is a rotation, not an index-wide liquidation: the Dow is down only 0.07% against a 1.37% Nasdaq Composite decline, energy led the eleven major sector groups while technology lagged, and the megacaps are split, with Apple up 1.37% and Meta down just 0.25% while Broadcom fell 4.88%, NVIDIA 3.01% and Micron 4.1%. The driver mix is genuinely two-sided. On the bearish side, chip weakness has broadened past Samsung's preliminary third-quarter results into a funding story, with reporting that Broadcom is arranging more than 50 billion dollars of financing for OpenAI chip purchases and Oracle pursuing a similar structure, which links the AI build-out to debt costs at a moment when CME FedWatch puts December hike odds near 67.9%; Oracle is down 4.9%. Oil remains the one amplifier still aligned with downside equity risk, with WTI near 91.31, up about 3.4%, and Brent near 104.05, up 3.84%, on shipping attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and a hurricane-related cut to US offshore output. On the supportive side, the long end eased, the 17:00Z sale of 30-year bonds cleared at a 5.618% high yield with a 2.54 bid-to-cover against a 2.41 average and a 0.1 basis point tail, removing an auction risk, and jobless claims at 197,000 against a 200,000 consensus showed no labour-market break. Under this provider's definition Tail measures the probability of a price path that denies meaningful mean reversion, not the size of a decline or the importance of a catalyst. Four independent price feeds hold their session lows, volatility and both yield tenors reversed lower, and megacap and sector breadth are split, so Tail is published at 22, in the watch band, one point above the previous hour only because the power hour and cash close remain ahead. Stress is 68 because a second consecutive lower session, a 3.66% semiconductor decline, Brent above 104, an active hiking cycle and an unresolved Iran conflict with weekend headline-gap potential describe a genuinely difficult environment that can still mean-revert. Confidence is 88: index, futures, ETF, semiconductor, volatility, two-year, ten-year and crude levels were each read from primary quote pages with explicit as-of stamps, the seven-day calendar and today's actuals were confirmed against a published calendar, and the Waller, AI-financing and Iran items were each read at source. Two items were checked and discarded: a live blog that proved to be dated July 7 rather than today, and a pre-close wire summary still citing a 5.34% ten-year that fresher direct quotes superseded. The shared Finviz context file was read as required, but its collection timestamp is 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z with partial status and unavailable futures and calendar sections, so it was treated as stale and excluded rather than allowed to stand in for live evidence.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours opened with a quiet mean-reverting overnight tape: Tail decayed from 14 at 19:00Z on October 7 to a cycle low of 10 at 03:00Z while Stress held a 47 to 51 range. From 06:00Z the oil and long-end-yield impulse took over, Tail stepping to 22 at 07:00Z and then holding a 20 to 23 watch-band range through the European and early US session as Stress climbed from 55 to a 60 to 66 plateau. The 14:00Z slot eased to 17 on an orderly US cash open before 15:00Z and 16:00Z returned to 20 and 22. The single block-band hour in the window is 17:00Z at Tail 28 and Stress 72, published on an observed failed retracement and extension to the session low; 18:00Z returned to 21 once a retracement was observed and holding. Dominant mode was mixed apart from trend-down readings at 06:00Z, 07:00Z, 11:00Z and 17:00Z. No published hour is rewritten here.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in the watch band at 22 for the 19:00Z power hour and 21 into the 20:00Z cash close, because a second leg would have to appear inside that window for the held low to fail. Tail then returns to the low band at 19 post-close and eases to 17 by 23:00Z. The named overnight checkpoint is the Asian handover: 00:00Z and 01:00Z are held at 20 because Tokyo and Seoul price today's 3.66% semiconductor decline and the AI debt-financing reporting for the first time, and a chip-led Asian second leg is the stated escalation mechanism. Risk then decays to a cycle trough of 16 between 05:00Z and 06:00Z as liquidity thins, before rebuilding to 18 at the 07:00Z European open and 19 through the US pre-market. It steps to 21 at the 13:00Z hour containing the 13:30Z US cash open and reaches a forward peak of 23 at 14:00Z, the only event/whipsaw slot, when preliminary Michigan sentiment and its inflation-expectation components print with a 4.6% prior one-year reading, Brent near 104 and the policy rate already at 3.75-4%. The final hours ease from 21 to 19 into the weekend, where the unresolved Iran conflict is carried as Stress and as Monday-open gap risk rather than as current-path Tail. Stress follows the same shape at a higher level, easing from 68 to 51 overnight and rebuilding to 66 around the Michigan print. Every slot beyond 19:00Z is conditional risk, not observed structure.
